article.title: Vue 3.6 Remains a Release Candidate at rc.16, With Vapor-Scoped Changelog Entries Swinging Between 19 and 49 Since rc.11
article.summary: Vue 3.6.0-rc.16 shipped November 20, six RCs after rc.11. The Vapor-scoped entry count has not kept falling: it swung from 19 to 49 and back across the interval.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

The Vue core team published v3.6.0-rc.16 on November 20, according to the [Vue core releases page](https://github.com/vuejs/core/releases/tag/v3.6.0-rc.16), which labels it a pre-release. It is the sixth release candidate since rc.11, which The Machine Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-10/10-vue-360-rc11-arrives-with-61-changelog-entries-59-of-them-scoped-to-vapor-mode-down-from-77-in-rc10) on October 10. Six weeks and five more RCs later, the decline in changelog entries that rc.11 appeared to continue has not held: by the Herald's tally of the [pre-release changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vuejs/core/v3.6.0-rc.16/CHANGELOG.md), the Vapor-scoped entry count fell to 19 at rc.12, rose to 38 at rc.13, fell to 24 at rc.14, then rose again to 49 at rc.15 and held at 48 at rc.16.

## What the Changelog Shows

Using the same method as the Herald's rc.11 article — counting changelog list items under Bug Fixes, Features and Performance Improvements, then counting how many carry a `compiler-vapor`, `runtime-vapor` or `vapor` scope tag — the six most recent release candidates break down as follows, per the [pre-release changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vuejs/core/v3.6.0-rc.16/CHANGELOG.md):

- rc.11 (October 10): 61 total entries, 59 Vapor-scoped
- rc.12 (October 16): 19 total entries, 18 Vapor-scoped
- rc.13 (October 23): 38 total entries, 35 Vapor-scoped
- rc.14 (October 30): 24 total entries, 23 Vapor-scoped
- rc.15 (November 12): 49 total entries, 32 Vapor-scoped
- rc.16 (November 20): 48 total entries, 45 Vapor-scoped

The gap between release candidates has also varied. The [changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vuejs/core/v3.6.0-rc.16/CHANGELOG.md) dates put six days between rc.11 and rc.12, seven between rc.12 and rc.13, and seven between rc.13 and rc.14, before the interval stretched to 13 days between rc.14 and rc.15 — the longest gap recorded across the whole release-candidate series so far — then shortened to eight days between rc.15 and rc.16.

Some of the entries point to specific work rather than just bug fixes. rc.14 added a feature described in the changelog as "add devtools component hooks," and rc.15 added one described as "track rendered teleports on instances for devtools." Both land under `runtime-vapor`. Vue's [Vapor Roadmap issue](https://github.com/vuejs/core/issues/13687) on GitHub lists "DevTools Integration" as an unchecked item under its Ecosystem section, and the issue's own last-updated timestamp, September 18, predates both of those devtools-related changelog entries — meaning the checklist has not been updated to reflect that work.

rc.15 also carried nine bug-fix entries scoped to `reactivity` rather than Vapor, covering issues such as a computed value that failed to notify its readers after invalidating itself and removed reactive links that kept younger effects from being garbage-collected. rc.16, meanwhile, included three entries — covering attribute fallthrough and server-rendering behavior for Vapor slot content — that describe Vapor-related interop work without carrying a `vapor`-prefixed scope tag themselves, a reminder that the scope-tag tally is an approximation rather than an exact count of Vapor-specific work.

## Stable Line Unaffected

Vue's stable 3.5.x line continues to ship in parallel. The [stable-line changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vuejs/core/main/CHANGELOG.md) lists 3.5.46 as published November 20 — the same day as rc.16 — with Vue 3.6 still not released to the stable line more than four months after rc.1 shipped on July 18, according to the [Vue core releases page](https://github.com/vuejs/core/releases/tag/v3.6.0-rc.16).

## What We Don't Know

- Neither the pre-release changelog nor the release pages reviewed give a date for a stable Vue 3.6.0 release or say how many further release candidates the team expects.
- The changelog gives no explanation for why the entry count rose and fell rather than declining steadily, and an entry count is not a measure of how severe or risky the underlying changes are.
- Whether the devtools-related Vapor features in rc.14 and rc.15 fully close the open "DevTools Integration" roadmap item, or represent partial progress toward it, is not stated in either the changelog or the roadmap issue.
